provenance.source: EOG fresh Azores yellow-eel endpoint plus upstream cleaned residency screen
provenance.eog_pattern: Layer-B world-support summary improved held-out receiver-week log loss from 0.1422727 to 0.1322871 and won 5/5 blocks despite a history-rich baseline.
provenance.interpretation_boundary: all values are hypothesis-generating associations; no causal pool state, hydrological driver, occupancy or movement path is identified

published_boundary: Restricted movement/pool fidelity is already reported by Verhelst et al. 2026 and is not the new target.
primary_question: Why do co-resident yellow eels show temporally persistent, locally clustered detection states despite no retained between-receiver movement?

hypotheses.name: pool_level_biological_state
hypotheses.primary_prediction: a shared pool-week component remains after individual history and observation heterogeneity are represented

hypotheses.name: receiver_tag_observation_state
hypotheses.primary_prediction: receiver/tag observation effects absorb same-pool covariance and reduce it toward the between-pool baseline

hypotheses.name: shared_biological_activity_rhythm
hypotheses.primary_prediction: co-resident eels show excess sub-weekly/diel synchrony after receiver operation is accounted for

hypotheses.name: hydrological_reset
hypotheses.primary_prediction: independently defined disturbance windows alter persistence or pool-level synchrony after H1-H3 decomposition

future_extension: Cross-system movement compression requires independent telemetry systems and is not inferable from Azores alone.
